Subject: Starter credits & commit tiers for NovaMed POC

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two quick questions as we prep procurement: 1) how do your starter/pilot credits apply to hosted API usage (are they per-token consumption credits or invoiced as a dollar offset)? 2) what do your commit tiers look like for per-token volume discounts — we expect a bursty pilot (peaks ~3M tokens/day, average ~600k/day) that could ramp if the POC goes well.

Specifically: can you outline a simple staging that includes an initial pilot credit, a mid-pilot commitment option, and the discounts that would kick in at 1M / 5M / 20M monthly tokens? Procurement will also want to know if unused credits expire or roll into first paid month.

We have a tight approval window for the POC (target start: second week of April). Any term sheet or short example cost model would help us move quickly.

Thanks —
Janelle

NovaMed


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Starter credits & commit tiers for NovaMed POC

Hi Janelle —

Great questions — appreciate the usage targets, that helps a lot. Quick summary below and I attached a short term sheet (NovaMed_POC_TermSheet_v1.pdf) and a simple model link. TL;DR: starter credits are applied as a dollar offset against hosted API usage (per-token billing converted to USD), they expire after 90 days unless a committed plan is signed that extends application windows.

Proposal (starter / staged commit):
- Pilot: 60-day POC with $15,000 starter credit applied to token usage (applies to first invoices until consumed).
- Mid-pilot commit option: If NovaMed signs a 3-month graded commit within the POC window (minimum $10k/month commit), we convert remaining credits into month-1 prepaid and lock a per-token discount schedule.
- Commit tiers (monthly aggregate tokens):
  - Tier A: up to 1M tokens/month — standard hosted rates (no additional discount beyond credits).
  - Tier B: 1M–5M tokens/month — 12% per-token discount off list hosted rate.
  - Tier C: 5M–20M tokens/month — 22% per-token discount.
  - Tier D: >20M tokens/month — negotiable, typically 30%+ depending on committed spend and SLA needs.

Unused credits: starter credits expire at 90 days from issuance unless NovaMed signs a 3–6 month commit; in that case we apply remaining credits pro rata against the first committed month(s).

Next steps
- If this aligns, I can send an updated term sheet (DocuSign) reflecting a $15k starter credit + optional 3-month commit conversion path.
- Laura/Marissa: looping you in for cost model and to confirm whether we should offer a one-time promotional bump for launch incentives.

Attachments: NovaMed_POC_TermSheet_v1.pdf (term sheet)

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Starter credits & commit tiers for NovaMed POC (internal)

Internal notes / negotiation posture — do not forward as-is to customer:

Rafael — I reviewed the term sheet and the simple model. Given NovaMed's expected bursty profile and the strategic value of a health-care reference, recommend we: 
1) Increase starter credit to $20k (one-time launch incentive) but require a 6-month graded commit option (month 1–2 $10k/mo; month 3–6 minimum $25k/mo) to unlock the Tier C (5M–20M) discount. This protects us from heavy initial burst without long-term commitment.
2) Make credits expire at 120 days if no commit signed, but allow pro rata conversion into month-1 prepaid once a commit is executed.
3) Offer an overage protection clause for the pilot: if tokens exceed 30M in any single month, auto-apply a protective rate to avoid unexpectedly high bills while we triage usage patterns.

Attachments: cost_model_novamed.xlsx (internal cost calculator) — Marissa, can you run the model with a 6-month ramp and confirm the net margin at the 22% discount level?

Also suggest we prepare an addendum: launch incentive clause that phases credits over the first two months (65% month 1, 35% month 2) to discourage front-loading.

Laura Bennett
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Please send the revised term sheet and DocuSign link; we aim to have signatures completed by Friday so the POC can start week of April 12. One question: can you confirm credits will be applied as dollar offsets on our hosted invoices (we want a clear invoice line item)?
